verses.text: And God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.

The fear and dread of you will fall on every living creature on the earth, every bird of the air, every creature that crawls on the ground, and all the fish of the sea. They are delivered into your hand.
Everything that lives and moves will be food for you; just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you all things.
But you must not eat meat with its lifeblood still in it.
And surely I will require the life of any man or beast by whose hand your lifeblood is shed. I will demand an accounting from anyone who takes the life of his fellow man:
Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man his blood will be shed; for in His own image God has made mankind.
But as for you, be fruitful and multiply; spread out across the earth and multiply upon it."
Then God said to Noah and his sons with him,
"Behold, I now establish My covenant with you and your descendants after you,
and with every living creature that was with you—the birds, the livestock, and every beast of the earth—every living thing that came out of the ark.
And I establish My covenant with you: Never again will all life be cut off by the waters of a flood; never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth."
And God said, "This is the sign of the covenant I am making between Me and you and every living creature with you, a covenant for all generations to come:
I have set My rainbow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth.
Whenever I form clouds over the earth and the rainbow appears in the clouds,
I will remember My covenant between Me and you and every living creature of every kind. Never again will the waters become a flood to destroy all life.
And whenever the rainbow appears in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of every kind that is on the earth."
So God said to Noah, "This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between Me and every creature on the earth."
The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. And Ham was the father of Canaan.
These three were the sons of Noah, and from them the whole earth was populated.
Now Noah, a man of the soil, proceeded to plant a vineyard.
But when he drank some of its wine, he became drunk and uncovered himself inside his tent.
And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father's nakedness and told his two brothers outside.

Then Shem and Japheth took a garment and placed it across their shoulders, and walking backward, they covered their father's nakedness. Their faces were turned away so that they did not see their father's nakedness.
When Noah awoke from his drunkenness and learned what his youngest son had done to him,
he said, "Cursed be Canaan! A servant of servants shall he be to his brothers."
He also declared: "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem! May Canaan be the servant of Shem.
May God expand the territory of Japheth; may he dwell in the tents of Shem, and may Canaan be his servant."
After the flood, Noah lived 350 years.
So Noah lived a total of 950 years, and then he died.

context.author: Genesis names no author. Jewish and Christian tradition, and the New Testament’s way of speaking of “the Law of Moses” (Luke 24:44), credit the five books of the Law to Moses. Many scholars think Genesis was gathered and shaped from older sources over a long time, and a few remarks look back from a later day: “at that time the Canaanites were in the land” (Genesis 12:6).
context.genre: Narrative of beginnings (Genesis 1-11): creation, the first family, the flood and the nations, with genealogies
context.audience: Israel, God’s covenant people, learning who their God is, where the world came from and what went wrong with it
context.setting: God blesses Noah and his sons: “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth” (v.1), the command of creation again. Now animals are given for food, but not with the blood still in it (vv.3-4), and human life is protected: “Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man his blood will be shed; for in His own image God has made mankind” (v.6). God makes a covenant with Noah, his descendants and every living creature: never again will a flood destroy the earth (vv.9-11). Its sign is the rainbow: “I have set My rainbow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth” (v.13). Then a darker scene: Noah plants a vineyard, gets drunk and lies uncovered in his tent (vv.20-21). Ham sees and tells his brothers; Shem and Japheth walk in backward and cover him (vv.22-23). Noah curses Canaan, Ham’s son, and blesses Shem and Japheth (vv.25-27). Noah dies at 950 (v.29).
context.custom: The Hebrew word for rainbow, qeshet, is the ordinary word for a warrior’s bow. Ancient Near Eastern art shows gods holding bows; here God hangs His bow in the clouds, a weapon set down. Blood stood for life itself (Leviticus 17:11), so it was to be poured out, not eaten, a rule still kept in kosher practice. Exposing a father’s nakedness was a deep shame in a culture of honor.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 10 lists the nations descended from Shem, Ham and Japheth, the Table of Nations.
context.timelineBible: The curse in v.25 falls on Canaan, not on Ham or his other sons, and it was later misused to defend slavery of Africans; the text gives no ground for that. The Jerusalem council asked Gentile believers to abstain from blood (Acts 15:20). Ezekiel’s vision of God’s glory is “like that of a rainbow in a cloud on a rainy day” (Ezekiel 1:28), and John sees a rainbow around God’s throne (Revelation 4:3).

translation.meaning: A bow, the archer’s weapon; also the rainbow. God sets His bow in the clouds.
Covenant. Seven times in vv.8-17: God binds Himself to every living creature, with no condition attached.
Image. After the flood, God grounds the value of every human life in the image of God (1:27).

gospelParallels.note: Abstain from blood and from what has been strangled.
A rainbow that gleamed like an emerald encircled the throne.
The authority bears the sword as God’s servant.

otBackground.note: The life of the flesh is in the blood.
As I swore the waters of Noah would never again cover the earth.
Like a rainbow in a cloud on a rainy day.

overview.summary: God renews the blessing of creation, guards human life because people bear His image, and makes a covenant with every creature never again to flood the earth, with the rainbow as its sign; then Noah gets drunk, Ham dishonors him, and Noah curses Canaan.
overview.settingLine: A new world after the flood.

history.t: A warrior’s weapon, hung in the clouds.
Ham’s son, ancestor of the peoples of the land.

customs.t: Blood is life, poured out, not eaten.
Covering a father’s shame showed respect.

archaeology.t: Wine jars with residue from about 6000 BC have been found in Georgia, in the Caucasus.
Assyrian reliefs show the god Ashur with a bow inside a winged disk.

overview.discussion: God sets His bow in the clouds and says, “I will remember My covenant” (v.15). When I see a rainbow, what promise of God do I want to remember?
overview.book: The book of Genesis · 50 chapters. Beginnings: creation, the fall, the flood and the nations, then God’s promise to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
overview.author: Moses, by tradition

peoplePlaces.d: Receives the covenant; plants a vineyard

timeline.label: Blessing and the value of life

historicalImage.caption: The Drunkenness of Noah, by Michelangelo (1509), Sistine Chapel, with the painted youths and medallions around it. Noah lies asleep while his sons cover him; at the left he digs in his vineyard (Genesis 9:20-23).
